events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $2.76 (model confidence 0.88)
events.body:
The trip is RydeTAXI, so the metered fare moves with the distance driven and an unexplained detour passes into what the rider pays [F6][RD-1]. The trace records one off-route segment, 18:46–18:52, 3.50 km driven where 1.54 km was optimal, +1.96 km (F3), and it is not screened out by any other clause [F3][RD-1].

RD-4 does not excuse it. The driver's claim of a breakdown and a slow road exists only in his post-trip statement [F8], which is a claim, not evidence. The only incident record, the 18:27 vehicle breakdown on the East Coast Parkway, is at 0 m from the optimal route and reported before the segment began [F11], but the trace settles that no qualifying incident sits on the replaced stretch, so RD-4(a) fails [F11][RD-4]. The speed-band records at 40–49 km/h (band 5) are well above the band 1–2 congestion definition and in any case cannot exempt a segment on their own [F9][F10][RD-4].

RD-5 consent for this segment: the in-app chat between rider and driver is empty [F7], so there is no rider message of any kind sent before 18:46:55 — no general route authorisation and no specific route. The only asserted agreement is the driver's statement, which under G11 is a claim, not consent [F8][RD-5]. A complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment means the segment counts, and RD-5's three scopes do not need to be reached [F7][RD-5]. The driver's alternate-route choice appears nowhere else in the record, so there is nothing tying the segment to any agreed road (G13 not triggered, because there was no agreement at all to scope) [F7][RD-5].

RD-3 stops: no stop is measured in this segment and the chat records no stop request, so the segment is not excused as a rider-named stop [F7][RD-3].

Amount [RD-2]: the rate is this fare record's distance fare divided by its distance km = $33.33 ÷ 23.64 km = $1.40989/km, as the trace states it. The trace fixes the billable extra km at 2.17 km ($3.06 at the stated rate) [F4]. The non-exempt segment's extra km is +1.96 km [F3]. 1.96 km × $1.40989/km = $2.7634, rounded to $2.76 (this reconciles with the trace's $3.06 where all 2.17 km were charged: 3.06 − 0.21 × 1.40989 = $2.76) [F3][F4][F6][RD-2]. Only the mileage unit of this segment is refunded; the waiting component of the fare is $0.00 and unaffected [F6][RD-2]. Surge is 1.0×, so nothing else is added or removed [F5][RD-2].

RD-6: the driver's profile shows 2 disputes in 90 days and 0 upheld, with route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so this case is not a repeated breach and no account flag is warranted [F14][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, the empty chat record, the driver's statement and the incident feed. Nothing threatens, intimidates, harasses or alleges dangerous driving [F7][F8][F11][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

Evidence: every element this ruling needs is present — the GPS segment measurement [F3], the fare records [F4][F6], the empty chat record [F7], the incident and speed-band records [F9][F10][F11], and both profiles [F13][F14]. Nothing is missing and the RD-5 finding does not change the outcome (it only fixes which segment counts), so no referral to a human is required.

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your trip and you're getting a partial refund of $2.76 as a Ryde voucher.

What decided it: on your RydeTAXI trip, the meter ran on distance driven, and the record shows one stretch between 18:46 and 18:52 where the route taken was about 1.96 km longer than the optimal route. Nothing else in the record excused that extra distance, so you were charged for it.

The $2.76 covers just that extra distance, at the same per-km rate as your fare. It's paid to you as a Ryde voucher, not cash or card. Nobody else needs to look at this, and your account isn't affected.

DRIVER: We reviewed the rider's dispute about this trip. Outcome: a partial refund of $2.76 to the rider as a Ryde voucher.

What decided it: the fare was metered on distance driven, and the GPS trace shows one stretch, 18:46–18:52, where about 1.96 km more was driven than the optimal route. There's no rider message before that stretch agreeing to a different route, and the breakdown and slow-traffic points you raised aren't supported by the incident or speed records for that stretch.

The $2.76 is taken against that extra distance only, at your fare's per-km rate. No account flag was applied, and your account stays as it is.
